scenes.heading: Writing a coaching agreement that sets clear expectations

sents.d: Writing a coaching agreement that sets clear expectations
A written agreement protects both the coach and the client relationship.
A coaching or consulting agreement should define session frequency and length, what's included (e.g. email support between sessions or not), cancellation and rescheduling policy, and payment terms.

Clarifying the difference between coaching and therapy or licensed advice — coaching is generally not a substitute for mental health treatment, legal advice, or financial advice — protects both parties and sets appropriate expectations about scope.

A cancellation policy (e.g. sessions cancelled with less than 24 hours notice are forfeited) protects your time and income from last-minute changes, and is standard practice most clients expect and respect once stated clearly.

take: Put scope, limits and cancellations in your coaching agreement.
